aboutMeContent.title: About Me
aboutMeContent.content:
Hello, I'm Üzeyir,

I'm a Computer Engineering graduate from Ege University. 
I have experience in technologies such as React, Flutter, MongoDB, MySQL, Node.js, etc.
I wrote my graduation thesis on multimodal deep learning-based automated Turkish radiology report generation from chest X-rays.
I'm currently working as an Intern Application Engineer at IBTECH (a QNB Bank subsidiary), developing enterprise applications with C# and Java for the bank's accounting ecosystems.
I'm not only developing my technical skills but also strengthening my communication abilities, leadership qualities, and teamwork compatibility through the events I actively participate in.

Throughout my university life, I took an active role in clubs like EKAMİT, IEEE, and BEST. 
With these clubs, I developed my organizational skills, learned how to work effectively with people from different fields, and contributed to many technical/social events.

I value personal development and being versatile. 
My hobbies include swimming, running, basketball, listening to music/podcasts, watching movies and TV series.
I currently have many hobbies, but the new things I want to try and learn are much more than what I have.

My career goal is to take part in big and impactful projects, have my contributions be visible, and have my name remembered with significant achievements.

My motto: 'Growth is where comfort ends; balance is hidden in every step.'
                                                                                                   -ChatGPT
(I asked it to generate a motto related to 'Golden Mean Theory' and 'stepping out of comfort zone'.)

For details, you can examine my 'resume', explore the 'Experience' folder, and reach me through the 'Contact Information' section on the left.

readMeFile.title: Read Me
readMeFile.content:
Welcome to My Website!!

About the Project
===========
The project: A personal website with a WinXP theme, working in both English and Turkish.
Some parts exist just for show (e.g., the 'My Computer' folder).
Even though most buttons don't do anything, I feel like I added some really fun stuff.
Many of them are easter eggs, and some behave differently depending on whether you view the site in English or Turkish.
Since I'm familiar with Turkish culture, I think I did a better job on that side.
You don't have to try too hard to find these easter eggs, but it might be fun if you do.
Please find them. I put a lot of effort into this project and those were the parts I enjoyed the most.

Why WinXP?
========
The year is 2008. I'm 5 years old. While playing football outside, I saw my dad coming home with some boxes.
Next to him was our neighbor, the one who used to play music for me on his computer.
Things came out of those boxes, but I had no idea what they were.
Until I saw the monitor... That's when I realized it was the same screen we listened to music on.
The first thing that greeted us was the classic WinXP background and interface.
After waiting impatiently, I asked my dad to play that song: Don Omar – Dale Don Dale.

I was allowed to play for one hour a day.
But my older brother must've gotten tired of me saying, 'Can you open the racing game, please?'
So after about 10 minutes, he'd kick me off the chair.
(I didn't know the difference between 1 hour and 10 minutes.)

Years went by... Games, cheat codes, internet cafés—little did I know this interface would leave such a lasting impression on me.

I built a few projects, but never released any of them. Then I got curious...
I wanted to make something public, so a website felt like the right choice.
Then I realized making it a personal portfolio in WinXP style—something meaningful to me—would boost my motivation.
And here we are...
